title: API 570 Training in Denver: Online Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep online for Denver piping inspectors: Commerce City unit piping, gas plant lines, CUI under snow and tracing, injection points and dead legs.
h1: API 570 Training in Denver: Piping Inspector Exam Prep for Refinery, Midstream and Contract Inspectors
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors in the Denver area

Piping inspection around Denver splits between one refinery and a large oilfield. Inside the fence at Suncor's Commerce City refinery there are crude, cracking, hydrotreating, sulfur and asphalt units joined by unit and offsite piping; north and east of the city, Weld County gas plants and crude stabilization facilities run their own process piping, and long-haul pipelines carry crude and products across the plains. Only part of that network is API 570 piping, and a Denver candidate needs to know where the boundary falls as well as how to inspect what lies inside it.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Denver. The API 570 course is online and self-paced, with an instructor answering your questions as you work through the codes. The American Petroleum Institute decides who is eligible, administers the piping inspector examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification to candidates who pass. Completing the course gets you ready for that examination; it does not stand in for it.

What the February 2027 and June 2027 windows examine

API publishes a Body of Knowledge and a Publications Effectivity Sheet for each set of windows, and the sheet for February 2027 and June 2027 is a useful reading list for anyone who works on Front Range piping. It names:

  • API 570, 5th edition (February 2024), the inspection code itself.
  • ASME B31.3, 2024 edition, for design, materials, welding, examination and leak testing of process piping; and ASME B16.5, 2020 edition, for flange ratings and dimensions.
  • API RP 574, 5th edition (February 2024) with Addendum 1, on piping inspection practice; RP 576 in part, on pressure-relieving devices; RP 577 on welding inspection and metallurgy; and RP 578 on material verification.
  • API RP 571, 3rd edition (March 2020), but only its definitions and fifteen listed mechanisms, among them amine stress corrosion cracking, corrosion under insulation, erosion, hydrochloric acid corrosion, mechanical and vibration-induced fatigue, soil corrosion, acidic sour water corrosion and sulfidation.
  • ASME Section V (2023 edition) Articles 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 23, the last for SE-797 thickness measurement only; ASME Section IX for welding; and listed articles of ASME PCC-2 (2022) on repairs.

The Body of Knowledge for the same windows spells out the calculations: pressure design thickness of straight pipe and permanent blanks under B31.3, corroded MAWP under API 570, hydrostatic and pneumatic leak test pressure, impact test exemption temperatures, preheat and heat treatment, thermal expansion, and flange working and test pressures. Later windows may change any of this, so check the sheet for the window you book.

Unit piping at a refinery built in three stages

Suncor dates its Plant 1 to 1931 and Plant 2 to 1937, and added Plant 3 in the 1970s for heavier crude; it bought the plants in 2003 and 2005 and operates them as one refinery of about 103,000 barrels a day. EIA's 2026 capacity survey still reports the site as Commerce City East and West, with vacuum distillation, catalytic cracking, catalytic reforming and hydrotreating of naphtha, jet, diesel and heavy gas oil, and Colorado's production capacity for sulfur, hydrogen and asphalt. Translated into piping services, that gives a Denver inspector most of the RP 571 list the exam uses.

Service on the siteMechanism on the examined RP 571 listWhat a circuit plan watches
Crude unit overhead lines and exchangersHydrochloric acid corrosionWhere water first condenses, and the piping just downstream of neutralizer or inhibitor injection
Hot crude, vacuum and gas oil linesSulfidationMaterial and temperature changes along the circuit, and any carbon steel component in an alloy system
Sour water, amine and sulfur recovery pipingAcidic sour water corrosion; amine stress corrosion crackingLow points, turbulence near pumps and control valves, and welds that were never stress relieved
Catalyst and slurry lines on the crackerErosion and erosion-corrosionElbows, tees and reducers downstream of high velocity
Heated asphalt, sulfur and traced linesCorrosion under insulationDamaged jacketing, tracer leaks and insulation that stays wet
Compressor and pump pipingMechanical and vibration-induced fatigueSmall-bore connections, unsupported branches and socket welds

A refinery with this history also has the piping problems that come with age and consolidation: tie-ins between plants that were once separate, lines whose service changed when units were linked, and records that began under several previous owners. None of that is exam content in itself, but it is exactly where API 570's rules on circuits, condition monitoring locations and records earn their keep.

Where API 570 stops on the Front Range

A good deal of the pipe a Denver inspector sees is not process piping, and the exam assumes you can tell the difference. Suncor's crude arrives partly through a transmission system from a storage facility at Guernsey, Wyoming, a route Suncor plans to strengthen with a new crude line under its Rocky Mountain Pipeline Project. DJ Basin crude leaves for Cushing on systems such as Saddlehorn and Grand Mesa, White Cliffs and Pony Express. ONEOK announced in 2024 a 230-mile, 16-inch refined products line from Scott City, Kansas, to Denver International Airport, adding 35,000 barrels a day to its Denver-area system, and trade press reported in August 2026 that the expansion was in service. Those are pipelines, inspected under federal pipeline safety rules and pipeline codes, not under API 570.

Upstream there is a third regime. Colorado's oil and gas regulator, the Energy and Carbon Management Commission, keeps a separate 1100 Series of flowline regulations in its rule book. Between the well and the long-haul pipeline sit the gas plants and stabilization facilities, and whether an owner inspects their process piping to API 570 is a choice of practice. The examination itself is written around refinery and chemical plant piping, so study it on those terms whichever side of the boundary you work on.

Corrosion under insulation in a dry, cold climate

Candidates from Denver sometimes assume CUI belongs to the Gulf Coast. The semi-arid climate does reduce the steady wetting that drives CUI near the sea, but Front Range sites have their own water sources: snow that melts into damaged jacketing, freeze-thaw cycles that open seams and sealant, steam tracing that leaks inside the insulation, and cold gas plant lines that sweat when warm air reaches them. Heated asphalt and sulfur lines add temperature cycling, which drives moisture in and out of the insulation.

The exam takes CUI from RP 571 and from API 570, which sets out where CUI inspection should concentrate and how much of a susceptible circuit to examine. Learn the temperature ranges and the inspection extents from the 5th edition text the exam uses rather than from older site procedures or rules of thumb, because candidates lose marks when they answer from memory of a previous edition. For field methods, see the guide to corrosion under insulation.

Injection points, mix points and dead legs

Refinery piping is full of places where something is added to a process stream: neutralizers and corrosion inhibitors into crude overhead systems, wash water ahead of hydrotreater effluent exchangers, and chemical injection on gas plant inlets. API 570 treats an injection point as a circuit of its own, extending upstream and downstream of the injection nozzle, with condition monitoring locations concentrated where the injected fluid meets and mixes with the main stream. Expect the exam to test the definition, how far the circuit extends, where the CMLs go and which inspection methods suit the job; the course works through the code text rather than giving you round numbers to memorise.

Dead legs are the other classic. Stagnant branches, idle bypasses, standby pump lines and capped tie-ins can corrode much faster than the active line, and API 570 expects them to be identified and inspected. In a Colorado winter a dead leg holding water has a second failure mode, freezing, which is one reason many owners prefer to remove a dead leg rather than monitor it indefinitely.

Worked example: hydrostatic test pressure for a replacement spool in winter

The Body of Knowledge asks you to calculate hydrostatic and pneumatic leak test pressures under B31.3 paragraphs 345.4 and 345.5. A typical open-book question looks like this.

  1. A replacement spool for a hot gas oil line has a design pressure of 400 psi at a design temperature where the allowable stress S is 16,500 psi. At the test temperature the allowable stress ST is 20,000 psi; both values come from Table A-1 or are given in the question.
  2. The basic hydrostatic test pressure is 1.5 times the design pressure, adjusted by the stress ratio when the design temperature is above the test temperature: PT = 1.5 × P × ST ÷ S.
  3. PT = 1.5 × 400 × 20,000 ÷ 16,500 = 1.5 × 400 × 1.212 = 727 psi.
  4. Check the result against anything else in the question that limits it, such as a flange rating from B16.5 or a stress limit at test conditions.

Winter adds two field questions the exam may also touch. B31.3 expects the test fluid to be water unless freezing or another adverse effect makes water unsuitable, in which case another suitable liquid may be used, and the material's toughness at the test metal temperature matters, which ties back to the impact test exemption curves the Body of Knowledge also lists. Practise both in the open-book PDF so you know where each rule sits.

Getting to API 570 from a Denver-area job

API looks for education plus experience in metallic piping inspection within the last 10 years, gained while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency; the API 570 certification requirements page explains the routes. The Front Range backgrounds that lead there most often are these.

  • Thickness and NDT technicians who run CML surveys on refinery and gas plant circuits. They already know SE-797 in practice; the step up is the engineering judgement behind corrosion rates and intervals.
  • Pipe welders and fitters, for example graduates of the welding programme at Red Rocks Community College in Lakewood, who bring B31.3 fabrication knowledge but need qualifying inspection years.
  • Pipeline integrity staff at Denver-area operators, whose pipeline experience may or may not count as process piping experience. Describe it accurately and let API decide.
  • Engineers, including graduates of Colorado School of Mines, who need one year of piping inspection to qualify.

Studying B31.3 between field days

Open-book speed comes from repetition in the PDF, not from reading the code cover to cover. Work each calculation type in the order the Body of Knowledge lists it, then switch to timed papers that copy the closed-book and open-book halves of the real exam. If you spend weeks at a time on DJ Basin sites, keep a running list of questions for the instructor so that nothing waits until the week before your window. Prometric lists test centres in and around Denver.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group in Denver

Refinery inspection departments, gas processors and contract firms can enrol several technicians and inspectors together; each works through the course at a pace that suits their rotation. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API in their own name, so sponsors should help candidates document their experience accurately rather than fill in applications for them.

faq.q: Can I attend API 570 training in person in Denver?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Denver or anywhere else: the API 570 course is studied online, at your own pace, with an instructor answering your questions. The only in-person day is the examination itself, which API runs at Prometric test centres once your application is accepted, and Prometric lists centres in and around Denver.

faq.q: Is the ONEOK line to Denver International Airport API 570 piping?
faq.a: No. A refined products line from Scott City, Kansas, to the airport is a pipeline, inspected under federal pipeline safety regulations and pipeline codes. API 570 covers in-service process piping such as the unit and offsite piping inside a refinery or chemical plant. Knowing which regime applies to which pipe is part of the judgement the exam expects.

faq.q: Does gas plant piping experience in Weld County count toward API 570?
faq.a: It may. API wants experience in metallic piping inspection gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency, and a gas plant's process piping is metallic piping in industrial service. Describe the circuits, methods and decisions you were responsible for on the application, and API will verify them. If you are unsure, ask API before you apply rather than after.

faq.q: Does corrosion under insulation really matter in Denver's dry air?
faq.a: Yes. Dry air reduces one source of moisture, but snowmelt, freeze-thaw damage to jacketing, leaking steam tracing and sweating cold lines all wet insulation on Front Range sites. For the exam, CUI comes from RP 571 and API 570 regardless of climate, so learn the code's temperature ranges and inspection extents from the edition on your effectivity sheet.

faq.q: Which RP 571 mechanisms should a Denver candidate study first?
faq.a: Start with the ones you meet locally and the exam lists: hydrochloric acid corrosion in crude overheads, sulfidation in hot gas oil lines, acidic sour water corrosion and amine stress corrosion cracking around sulfur recovery, CUI, and vibration-induced fatigue on compressor piping. Then cover the rest of the fifteen listed mechanisms, because the exam does not weight questions by what your plant runs.

faq.q: Is ASME Section V Article 23 on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Only one part of it. The effectivity sheet for February 2027 and June 2027 lists Article 23 for SE-797, the standard practice for ultrasonic thickness measurement by the manual pulse-echo contact method. If you already take thickness readings for a living, expect questions on calibration, couplant, temperature effects and doubling, and check the article's wording rather than your site's habits.

faq.q: I work on Suncor's site for a contractor. Should I take API 570 or API 510 first?
faq.a: Take the one that matches the work you are doing and the experience you can document. If most of your scopes are piping circuits, API 570 is the natural first certificate; if you mostly inspect drums, columns and exchangers, start with API 510. Either one later qualifies you automatically for API 580 if you move toward risk-based inspection.

faq.q: Can a Denver contractor enrol its UT technicians for API 570 preparation?
faq.a: Yes. Groups can enrol together, with each technician studying at their own pace and putting questions to the instructor. Fees are quoted on request. Each technician still needs qualifying experience and an individual application to API, so check eligibility first; for the crew's NDT qualifications, see NDT training for Denver technicians.
